name: claude-haiku-5-5 on prompts/insight-41.txt
reply: Arthur Scammell wrote the song in 1928 about squid-jigging fishermen in Newfoundland, and this recording is a version of it [W1]. It is sung to the traditional Irish jig tune Larry O'Gaff, and its melody matches the Flanagan Brothers' 1927 recording Mick from Tralee [W2][G3]. The song is about squid jigging, where bait squid are caught with a baitless metal jigger of tiny hooks, on inshore grounds usually from July into August [G6][G8]. Dick Nolan is a Newfoundland folk performer known for Toronto nightclub work [L1][L2], but the sources I have don't mention his recording of this song, so its details are not documented here [W6][G5].

name: claude-haiku-5-5 on prompts/insight-1.txt
reply: Sundown was issued as a single in 1974 and became Gordon Lightfoot's only number one on the US Hot 100 [W1][W3]. He said the lyrics came from wondering what his girlfriend was doing out with friends while he wrote at home, and he tied the song to his roughly three-year relationship with Cathy Smith [W5][G4]. Despite its mellow sound, it is described as dark, expressing jealousy and paranoia [G3].
